CHN.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Implement the already-announced matching 25% on the remaining ~$16B when USTR List 2 takes effect on 23 August, and state clearly that a $200B List 3 — especially at 25% — will draw a prepared mix of remaining tariff space and qualitative measures. Do not launch unforced new tariff waves or a managed devaluation now, and do not revive the May purchase-commitment package unless Washington freezes List 3. Keep a negotiating channel open so a pause remains available if the U.S. wants one.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The threat is high but not existential. List 1 ($34B at 25%) is already in force with matching Chinese retaliation the same day (2018-07-06); USTR published List 3 (~$200B, ~6,000 lines) on 2018-07-10 and on 2018-08-01 said it is considering raising that rate from 10% to 25%; List 2 (~$16B at 25%) was finalized 7 August for 23 August. Section 301 is aimed at industrially significant / Made in China 2025 sectors, not consumer odds and ends. The April ZTE denial order showed U.S. component leverage over a major Chinese telecom, and the 13 August NDAA ban on U.S. government/contractor use of Huawei and ZTE continues firm-level tech pressure even after the commercial ZTE ban was lifted in July. FX is the clearest stress channel: DEXCHUS moved from ~6.34 in late February to 6.933 on 15 August (~9.4% weaker), the broad dollar is up ~7%, and Trump has already accused China of currency manipulation — so further engineered depreciation would invite a currency-war charge and capital-flight risk. That said, this is not +1.0: industrial production is still ~6% y/y (106.1), SA merchandise exports have not collapsed, and reserves remain ~$3.13tn with only about a 1% decline. Action should therefore be proportional retaliation, not maximal escalation or concession. China cannot match $200B+ in U.S. goods; the 19 May joint statement (China to “significantly increase” purchases; Mnuchin “on hold”) was discarded by the White House on 29 May; and analysts have judged a 2015-style devaluation too costly. Matching List 2 preserves credibility. Holding extra qualitative tools until List 3 is actually imposed avoids handing Washington a pretext for another $200B tranche, while talks can still be used to test a freeze.
key_factors: List 1 live and List 2 locked for 23 Aug; List 3 $200B may rise from 10% to 25%
Section 301 / MIC2025 targeting plus ZTE near-shutdown and NDAA Huawei/ZTE government ban
Yuan ~9.4% weaker (DEXCHUS 6.933 on 15 Aug) with currency-manipulation accusations
China cannot tariff-match $200B+ of U.S. goods; May purchase truce collapsed in 10 days
Real economy still holding: IP ~6% y/y, exports not collapsing, reserves ~$3.13tn

sources_cited.excerpt: List 1 tariffs take effect: US 25% on ~$34B of Chinese goods. China imposes matching ~$34B retaliation the same day.
USTR publishes proposed List 3: ~$200B of Chinese imports for an additional 10% tariff (~6,000 product lines).
At Trump's direction, USTR says it is considering raising the proposed List 3 rate from 10% to 25%.
US and China release joint statement after talks: China agrees to "significantly increase" purchases of US goods and services. Mnuchin says trade war is "on hold."
White House announces the US will proceed with Section 301 actions, including 25% tariffs on ~$50B of Chinese imports. Truce collapses.
US Commerce Department bans ZTE from buying US components (denial order). ZTE faces operational shutdown. Major non-tariff escalation.
China industrial production still 106.1 (same period previous year = 100) as of 2018-08-01.
China reserves ex-gold ~$3.129tn as of 2018-08-01, down about 1% over the window.
On August 7, 2018, USTR finalized a list of $16 billion of imports from China at 25%, effective August 23, 2018.
Trump signs NDAA measure banning US government and contractors from using Huawei and ZTE technology.
Analysts warn yuan depreciation as a trade-war tool would be too costly given capital-flight and 2015 risks.
